 <observation>Title: Cloning and characterization of CLIC2, a novel gene encoding a protein with homology to a intracellular chloride channel.
Authors: D L Heissmeyer, H M Seipel, H R Schneider, A Poustka
Journal: Genomics
Year: 1997
Abstract: We have cloned and sequenced a novel cDNA, CLIC2, that maps to the human chromosome region Xq28. The clone was identified in a search for human orthologues of the sea urchin receptor for egg jelly (suREJ1). The complete cDNA has a length of 1152 bp and contains an open reading frame of 741 bp. The deduced amino acid sequence predicts a protein of 247 amino acids with 64.9% similarity and 55.4% identity to bovine NCC27, a putative intracellular chloride channel protein. Furthermore, a 28 amino acid region shows 46.4% similarity and 28.6% identity to suREJ1. Northern blot analysis revealed high expression of the CLIC2 gene in skeletal muscle and low expression in lung, kidney, heart, and placenta. Database searches identified the complete genomic sequence of CLIC2 on a published PAC clone, allowing the determination of the exon-intron structure of the gene, which spans a genomic region of about 105 kb and consists of seven exons.
PMID: 9339381
